utterances.text: On page 3, paragraph 3, you say that you saw Serbs in uniform torching Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is that -- is it, however, true, Mr. Avdic -- torching anyone's house is tragic, and I'm not going to comment on that, I'm just asking you about the facts. But is it true that the first houses that were set on fire in Foca were Serb houses?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: No. They were not the first to be torched.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And do you know that the Muslims first set fire to Serb houses in the settlement of Donje Polje?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that among the first Serb houses to burn were the houses of Milorad Krnojelac, the Drokula family, the Stankovic family, et cetera? Is that true or not? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know whether they were among the first, but I do know that Milorad Krnojelac's house, who was then the warden of the KP Dom, that prisoners who went to repair the house, prisoners from the prison went to repair Milorad Krnojelac's house, and on the basis of what they told us, that they had learned from his wife and children that their house had been set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And for the Drokula, Stankovic, and other family homes that were set on fire at the very beginning, they were Serb homes. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What little you do know you only know from what Muslim -- other Muslims in prison told you. So you didn't see a single Serb house burning?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact location of -- of individual Serbs in Foca, but they were only in the southern part of Donje Polje, inhabited mostly by Muslims, and Donje Polje was burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But my question was did you know of Serb houses that were burnt, apart from this one that you described? Let's leave that one out. But do you know of any other Serb houses burning?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: I just said that I didn't know the exact location of Serb houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You don't know of any burnt Serb house except this one?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: There may be some, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Probably that is the reason why you don't mention the torching of Serb houses, because you didn't know about them. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you are asserting that Serb forces were wearing JNA uniforms, do you know that each member, if he was a military conscript in the former SFRY, was issued a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: I was not militarily involved or engaged because I was proclaimed unfit to serve in the Yugoslav People's Army so that I don't know these things. I was only active in the Civil Defence. And I also had an appropriate uniform of the Civil Defence, but this is quite different; it is blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know that military conscripts had JNA uniforms in their homes?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you yourself, on page 3, paragraph 4, claim that you saw locals, people from Foca, wearing JNA uniforms; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Serbs, Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Locals of Foca in JNA uniforms. Where did they get JNA uniforms when there was no JNA unit near Foca except for those 12 soldiers in Filipovici guarding the warehouse? So is the reason what I just said?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: They probably obtained all that equipment earlier on from the Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And is it beyond dispute, because you say there were citizens of Foca wearing JNA uniforms, that they were members of the local Territorial Defence and not members of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Now, whether they were local TO, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you're talking about citizens of Foca, and there were no JNA units in town, so surely they must be Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: There were some people I didn't know by their appearance but only on the basis of their speech. When I walked around Foca, I made the conclusion, in view of the fact that they spoke Ekavian, that they came from the teritory of Serbia, whereas the people of Foca all use the Ikavian dialect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, that is certainly quite true that the people of Foca use that dialect, but you identified those from Serbia as being members of paramilitary units that you have listed, so I don't need to list them again.

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Both.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. On page 3 in your statement, paragraph 6, you say that on the 19th of May, 1992, when you were going to visit your mother's house, you were arrested by an armed soldier with a light machine-gun, wearing an olive-grey uniform; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In Avdic, in addition to this statement which I'm quoting from which you gave to the investigators on the 16th and 17th of October, 1995, you gave another statement to the Centre of Security Services of Sarajevo on the 12th of October, 1994; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When talking of your arrest, on page 2 of that statement, in the last paragraph you say that on the 19th of May, you were arrested by the police. Here you say a soldier --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. It's tab 23. Has the witness got a copy of it? Let him have a copy of that statement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just finish my question, Mr. May, so as to be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The police, or to be more precise, the military police, isn't that so?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Yes, in uniform, SMB uniform of the former Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, please, who arrested you; a soldier, a policeman, or a military policeman?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: A military policeman wearing the uniform of the Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On what basis did you come to the conclusion that he was a military policeman and not a soldier?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: He himself told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what colour was the belt he was wearing and the other equipment on him, not the uniform?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: I didn't pay any attention. I was quite beside myself with fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you do know that the military police differ from ordinary soldiers because they don't wear brown belts but white belts and cross belts. Were they white or not?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I said that I couldn't really see even properly out of fear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you -- so you couldn't even see the man who arrested you.

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: I saw his face, but I was hardly conscious.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, judging by what you concluded, was he a member of the JNA, the local TO, the Army of Republika Srpska, or whom did he belong to?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Avdic, in the KP Dom in Foca, you were detained until the 5th of October, 1994; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And you were then exchanged?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, I'm asking you about your personal experience because I see that you spent a long period of time in the KP Dom. Were you mistreated while you were there?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: I personally was not physically mistreated by anyone, but psychologically and other types of mistreatment - I had no contact with my family, no medicines, hunger, fear, eternal fear, cold - all this is mistreatment, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Of course it is. I am not disputing that, but I asked you whether you personally were physically mistreated in any way.

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours. That was not the first question. The question was, "Did anyone mistreat you at all?" It was more general.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let me repeat that question. Did anyone mistreat you apart from what you said; cold, hunger, poor conditions?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Physically, no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. On page 4, paragraph 3, you say that at the beginning the guards in the KP Dom were mixed, both locals and people from the outside. Is that what you say?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You claim that among the guards there were members of the Serb guards. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Who were those people? Who were they?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: People from Serbia proper wearing uniforms. On the basis of a statement by my colleague who, with his family, was shut up in the KP Dom as soon as the camp was formed, and some 20 days later they were released from the KP Dom, and then when they visited me, we exchanged visits in our homes, they told me that there were people from the outside who were armed, wearing uniforms, who were guarding them initially, in the initial period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But you didn't see those people from the outside, did you?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: In the KP Dom, no, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's all I wanted to check, because you know about the presence of people from the outside from somebody else's stories.

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: With respect to the KP Dom, yes, but not with respect to Foca as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And according to those stories, they were replaced by locals who used to work in the KP Dom before when it was a civilian prison; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: As far as you are concerned, however, you only saw people from Foca who were there.

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Maybe the question is superfluous because, indirectly, you already answered it, but I would like to clarify it. Among the guards or in the administration of the KP Dom, was there anyone from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: In the administration, I don't know. In the administration building I went only once, when I wanted to intervene with the prison warden. I was in his office, and that is the only time I entered that building. So I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So I see you can't tell us anything about that. Let me now ask you a few brief questions which can all be reduced to a single one. You mention in your statement quite a large number of names when talking about Serbs. You mention a certain forester, Sumar. Is he a man from Foca?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You mention somebody called Todorovic on page 6, paragraph 7.

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is he from Foca?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Then you mention a certain Rasovic in the sixth paragraph, page 6, paragraph 7. Is he from Foca?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: He lived in Foca. Now, whether he was a native of Foca, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm talking about the citizens, the inhabitants of Foca. You also mention a certain Burilo, Koroman, Obrenovic, Matovic, Miocevic, Pljevaljcevic, Cancar, Vukovic. Are they all people from Foca?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were guards at the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So all locals from Foca itself. And a certain Savic and Maric, Stevanovic, Solaja, Pejic. Are they all from Foca too?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were guards in the KP Dom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So all these people that you had contact with during your detention in the KP Dom were locals of Foca?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Avdic. I have no more questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have very little to ask this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Avdic, you were exchanged on the 5th and 6th of October?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: On the 6th in the morning. We left Foca on the 5th, and on the 6th in the morning we were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: I see. You left on the 5th, you reached close to Sarajevo, as you said here, and at Kule, close to Sarajevo, you saw two armed Chetniks, as you said here, and then later on, when they took you back to Rogolj, again you saw 30 armed Chetniks but the bus didn't stop. And then again in Miljevina when you met the new KP Dom warden, he entered with Chetniks the nearby house and they spoke for about an hour. My question is: What did you mean when in these three cases you referred to armed Chetniks? What did you mean under that term? Who were those men?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: They were wearing uniforms. They were all Serbs. When they brought us to Kula for the exchange, we didn't get off the bus. Those two armed Chetniks with machine-guns, wearing uniforms of the Yugoslav army, ordered the guide from Foca who was taking us to Sarajevo to take us back to Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: But excuse me, you said as follows: On the way to Rogolj, we saw 30 Chetniks armed but the bus didn't stop. How then could you come to any conclusions as to who those men were, where they were from if you didn't get off the bus at all.

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: That was on the way back from Sarajevo towards Miljevina. There's a restaurant up there on this hill, and on the basis of stories, they just greeted the driver and the escort who was escorting us. This group that was in the building and outside the building next to the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: So these 70 men that you referred to that were detained in the correctional facility were all exchanged on the 6th?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: A few questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Mr. Avdic, you were asked in the course of your cross-examination about barricades erected in Donje Polje in the first few days of the attack on Foca. In those first few days did you leave your apartment building?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: Out of fear. I was afraid they would kill me. I didn't want to be killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Were you staying in your apartment or elsewhere in the apartment building?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: We were hiding in the cellar, in the basement of the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: You were asked, Mr. Avdic, or you gave evidence in cross-examination about planes flying over Foca. Can you tell us, please, when you saw planes flying over Foca?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: I saw that after the fall of Foca, which is to say seven or eight days later. I can't be precise. I saw planes flying down the Drina from the Pluzina direction, from the north, about 25 kilometres from Foca, or, rather, to the south of Foca. And they were flying down the Drina River flowing towards the north. This was a military plane, an air force plane, from Gorazde and that part.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. Avdic, did you come across in your time in Foca someone by the name of Marko Kovac?

utterances.speaker: SAFET AVDIC
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. PACK
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to note the witness was asked about Donje Polje. If I can note the reference in the Kunarac transcript to earlier evidence about the burning of houses there, the reference is transcript pages 661 and following. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Avdic, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the International Tribunal to give it. You are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution calls the next witness, Mr. Juso Taranin. Mr. Taranin has an unusual set of protections being that he has not requested a pseudonym but has requested, and has been granted from the previous trial, facial distortion. So we have the inconvenience of just setting up the blind before he's brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we're waiting for the witness to be brought in, may I request a number for the exhibit of binder of three exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Have we a summary in this case?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we do not have a summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You're going to simply ask the witness some questions to start with, are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was just going to draw the Chamber's attention to page 3.005 of the transcript. This witness was called to be cross-examined on the JNA involvement. I would point out to the Chamber what that was. He testified previously about going to a military warehouse of the JNA seeking protection. He will discuss the guards that he saw there. He will talk about Major Muharem Kurtovic who was mentioned in the last cross-examination. He has also testified previously about the arrival of people he described as Chetniks, about how they exerted some command over the JNA soldiers present at the warehouse, and finally, he has described in his prior testimony the killing of seven men at that warehouse. That is the portion of the testimony that I believe is in controversy. I have explained to the witness that I would not ask him any questions or read any summary before his testimony. He will simply be asked questions by the accused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If you would stand, please, and take the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Please take a seat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Taranin, the Chamber has before it the prior testimony that you gave in another proceedings before the International Tribunal. I will not ask you any questions now, but you will be asked questions by Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Taranin, in addition to the statement you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. gave to the investigators on the 4th and 5th of May, 1995, you also gave another statement in Skopje on the 11th of July, 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I have the statement here in front of me. I was given it along with the one you gave to the investigators. Tell me, please, who is this man Vahid Bogunic whom you gave the statement to in 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: He's a man, an officer it seems that he was of the Yugoslav army, and that's what he asked me. I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So it was somebody who took down your statement in Skopje. This man was an officer of the JNA, is that it?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In that statement, you said that on the 18th of April, you found yourself in the village of Filipovici in the military depot of the JNA warehouse; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in -- you arrived in that JNA warehouse because you believed that you, just like the other civilians who happened to find themselves there, that you'd be protected, find protection there?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Filipovici is a village 12 kilometres away from Foca; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, I can't say exactly how many kilometres, but it's around eight, ten, 12, thereabouts. I never measured the distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that as far as the JNA guards standing guard over that warehouse, there was a total of 12 soldiers providing security?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't know how many, but soldiers were there and there was an officer there, too, from Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But you don't know that there were just 12 soldiers stationed there?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't know how many soldiers, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know what kind of warehouse it was?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't know that either. All I know is that it was up in the hills because I have a weekend cottage nearby, near the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And do you know that it was in fact a fuel depot and military equipment warehouse, but no weapons or anything there except for those used by the soldiers guarding the place?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in the warehouse, along with those 12 soldiers there, and you say you don't know how many of them were there, as their officer and a man in charge of the warehouse, generally speaking, there was a JNA major by the name of Muharem Kurtovic?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, and I know him well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. And is this true too, that you said that around 1800 hours on that same day, a group stormed the JNA warehouse of about 80 members of the Serb guards, is that right, who had on their caps the cockades, crosses, or something like that?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: What they had on their caps, I can't say. I didn't know about those things much, but I think they had cockades and the flag too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, I don't suppose you're challenging the fact that the people that stormed the warehouse were not in fact JNA members?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I consider that they were, because they were wearing uniforms of soldiers who were also with them of the -- of that former army of yours -- of ours, sorry, of ours, and the ones wearing camouflage uniforms, the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You also say in your statement given in Skopje that the commander of the unit, the leader of the unit, you're talking about the people who arrived, you say a unit of the Serb guards arrived. So not the JNA. And that's what it says in paragraph 3. And then you go on to say that the commander of the unit with another few individuals went to see Major Kurtovic and they negotiated with them. And during that time, the rest engaged in preparation to -- the soldiers, for them to leave the barracks, as you refer to this military facility.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I think that it also says -- I think what it says in the statement is what I said, and I stand by it. I stand by what I said in my statement, and I think it's all written down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, the soldiers and the guards. These soldiers and the guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm only quoting from your statement. That's all I'm doing, nothing else. So you say that the commander of that unit, the unit that arrived with this insignia, these 80 men, went to negotiate with Major Kurtovic. Do you know what they were negotiating?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, is it true and can we deduce from this that the members of that paramilitary unit loaded up the soldiers onto a truck, or rather, evicted them from the facility and drove them off in an unknown direction?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No. Those soldiers were there. How they left, I really can't say. I don't know. But they mistreated us there. They beat us. They killed some people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But not JNA soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, the guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's why I'm saying this. Major Kurtovic, you say yourself, left that place in his own private car, drove off in his own car; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I didn't see it happen, and I couldn't see it, but most probably he did leave. I didn't see him do it because we were -- we had our hands up in the air, had to keep them raised. And we were put up against this hangar and we weren't allowed to move at all. Some people were shot there and goodness knows what else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. But in your statement, you say that Major Kurtovic's soldiers with their own sidearms were loaded up onto the truck and driven off. And Major Kurtovic left the warehouse, the barracks, as you say, in his own car which was a Golf.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, probably. I don't know really.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And not a single one of his soldiers shot a single bullet. So this small unit of 12 men were evicted from the JNA warehouse.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No. They were all there together. They weren't evicted, forced out. Them and the soldiers, they seem to be the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, Mr. Taranin. Well, is it true that somebody standing guard in front of the warehouse could have left their posts unless they were forced to, and they couldn't have been forced to had there been any serious JNA unit there in the Foca region at that time. Who would have dared to evict the guards from the warehouse and Major Kurtovic?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to enter into that subject. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's not, then. Let's not pursue the point. You go on to say that you saw that the members of this paramilitary unit shot seven Muslims, is that right, on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That has nothing to do with the JNA soldiers. You say of them in this statement that they did not take part in that; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: They stood to the side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They were thrown out of there?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, they weren't thrown out. They were there. They were moving around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They were loaded onto vehicles and driven off, that's what you say.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, we were loaded onto vehicles and they probably, after us, followed. The guards were put on buses too, and together with us they arrived at Velecevo, where they had taken us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did those soldiers come with them or not?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't know about the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You say Kurtovic, the soldiers of Major Kurtovic, with their sidearms, were loaded onto vehicles and driven off. Major Kurtovic left the barracks in his private passenger car of the Golf brand.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Possibly. I see. In your statement that you gave to the investigators, on page 2, paragraph 5, you say that you saw some ten days prior to this attack on Foca when you say that the Serbs took control of Foca, members of the JNA came into town in their private cars to distribute weapons to the local Serbs. Is that what you said in your statement?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now tell me, please, why you did not mention those allegations in your statement given in Skopje in June 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: How do I know? I didn't know this officer, so I didn't have much contact with him. I didn't know him. He came to my room.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: You see that his name was Bogunic Vahid. He was obviously a Muslim. So what was the problem; you didn't trust him?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I didn't, because I had left this Golgotha out of fear. I didn't trust him. I didn't believe him about his name or anything else, but he persuaded me to make this statement, so I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Since you say in the statement that you now confirmed and which I quoted from on page 2, paragraph 5, that members of the JNA came in private cars and distributed weapons, how did you know that they were JNA members if some people came in private passenger cars and distributed weapons?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Not in private cars, but a two-tonne truck with a tarpaulin arrived. And this officer and the soldiers who brought this in front of my building gave the weapons out, and all those who took the weapons entered the building. They didn't conceal anything. This was happening in front of the building I lived in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But I'm asking you on the basis of your statement, because you said on page 2, paragraph 5, that they came in civilian cars and that they distributed weapons. Is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: In private cars, no. It wasn't like that. A small truck arrived, and that's how it was. That's what I said in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Fine. I'm just drawing your attention to paragraph 5, page 2 of your statement to the investigators. We can move on, because I don't want to waste any more time. Those men who arrived in those cars, were they wearing JNA uniforms?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe those uniforms?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: The uniforms of the former Yugoslav army, olive-green uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Green-grey SMB uniforms?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, the ordinary regular uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, does this indicate that they were certainly members of the TO, the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps. I don't know. I saw soldiers and a lower-ranking officer, but I don't know who he was. They didn't hide anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's why I'm saying that in view of the uniform, there must have been members of the Territorial Defence because they wore ordinary olive-green/grey uniforms. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I had such a uniform in my own apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Because I was a member of the Territorial Defence as a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's very good. I won't ask you any more about that. So we'll move on to my next question. On page 2, paragraph 8, you say that on the 8th of April, from the surrounding hills, the attack on Foca started and that the conflict went on, according to the previous witness, eight to ten days. He can't say exactly how long it lasted. How long did it last according to you, how many days?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I can't tell you for certain, because I left. That night when there was the conflict, it wasn't really a conflict. It was fear that had spread through our bones, and I left my house and went to my weekend home at Ustikolina near to the military facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I understand that, but do you have any knowledge as to how long it lasted, how many days?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Maybe more than ten days, but there was no major conflict. I don't know that there was any.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: If there was no major conflict, why then did the Serbs need more than ten days to take control of Foca if there was no conflict?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: How do I know? The Serbs took Foca in 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So was it in 24 hours or eight to ten days? Make your mind up.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, from the hills. But the town was taken over by the Serbian police, the post office as well. And what else then? They were across the Drina. On one side there was the Serb army, what kind of army it was, I don't know. I didn't see them. And on this other side, I have no idea who was on the other side. There was just shooting just like that for no particular purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you mean the Muslim side was shooting just like that?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Well, there was nothing to shoot at. No one was defending it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Nobody was defending Foca? So no one was defending it, and it took the Serbs ten days to take control of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But I'm telling you, they took it over in 24 hours. The police took it over and everything was over.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Taranin. And who was fighting who?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. He's answered that. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge which positions were held by Muslim forces in Foca during those conflicts?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I have no idea that they held positions anywhere in Foca and around Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know anything at all even when you say that they were shooting just like that. From what positions were they shooting just like that as you put it, these members of the Muslim forces? From which positions?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I don't know that they had any positions. I don't know that they had any positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, they must have shot from somewhere, even if it was without any reason or cause.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're going round in circles, and the witness said that he can take the matter no further than he has done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything at all about artillery firing on Serb positions by Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: There weren't any, nor was there any artillery because so many people wouldn't have fled if they had that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The previous witness said there was some, only the shells didn't go off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness can't answer for what some other witness said. He said there wasn't any, this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. May. He said both. He is not disputing the fact that they were shooting, only he says that they were shooting just like that, but even that he can't tell us where from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell me, do you know the part of town known as Donje Polje?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, only I was in Gornje Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you don't know anything about any military operations from that part of town?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: No, nothing. I was in the basement. I know nothing about that. I just heard the shooting and that's all, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The fighting in Foca, was it between local Serb and Muslim forces in Foca?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I can't tell you that either, because I don't know. I don't think that they were locals. I think they were all from the outside, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, in your opinion. I'm not asking you of your opinion, I'm asking you about facts. Tell me, did you notice a single JNA member or any JNA unit that was participating in the fighting in Foca, the fighting that continued from the 8th up until the 16th or 20th of April, I don't know. Did you -- my question is: Did you notice a single JNA unit involved in the fighting in Foca? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: It says what I said in my statement, and I know nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: My question is quite specific. Did you notice a single unit or member of the JNA participating in the fighting in Foca from the 8th to the 16th of April? Did you notice any?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I noticed tanks and cannon and everything along the Drina towards Scepan Polje and Brod on the Drina. I noticed them moving.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Where were they moving to?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: They were moving towards Scepan Polje up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the conflict in Foca.

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: The conflict in Foca? I can't tell you anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So you can't tell me anything. Very well. In that conflict, were the same units involved that had broken into the JNA warehouse when you were there?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On page 3, paragraph 8, you say that the commander of this paramilitary unit was accompanied all the time by a soldier who was about 60 years old who had a grey beard; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: He was an officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And he wore a camouflage uniform; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes. The camouflage uniform that soldiers everywhere wear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And is it clear to you, in view of his experience and his grey beard and his 60 years of age, that he couldn't have been an officer or soldier of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: He was probably an active-duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see an active-duty officer with a grey beard, or any kind of beard, for that matter, in the JNA? Did you see such a person ever? Did you ever hear of any such person?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: While Tito was alive, they couldn't -- weren't allowed to wear any beards or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And do you know that anyone was ever allowed in the JNA or the Army of Yugoslavia to wear a beard?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: They were probably reserve officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let me shorten this. Since this question of private cars and grey beards is still disputed: During your stay in the KP Dom in Foca, did you notice anyone over there that was a member of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I couldn't see when I was in the building. I didn't go out. They wouldn't let us go out. So what could I see? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since you didn't see anything, do you know at all that all the personnel came from the local population? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I only saw policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were they also locals?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: I didn't know any one of them. A few of them. They were former policemen who held the KP Dom, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: From Foca?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Where they were from, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I see. You don't know that either. Very well. On page 5 of the statement to the investigators, in paragraph 3 you say that Chetniks, as you put it, came to the bus stop while you were waiting with your wife for the bus in order to leave Foca; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When you explain that in those terms, is it at least true that even then you didn't notice among them a single member of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: They were soldiers, real soldiers, as they say, in those camouflage uniforms, and they were shooting up above our heads.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Taranin, that the only JNA soldiers that you saw during those events you are testifying about were those soldiers of Major Kurtovic in the warehouse? Is that right or not, Mr. Taranin?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: As I was saying, there were these people who came, and there were these others who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: My question is a very precise one: Is it true that the only JNA soldiers is that you saw throughout that period were Major Kurtovic's soldiers in the warehouse where you had sought shelter? Is that right or not, Mr. Taranin?

utterances.speaker: JUSO TARANIN
utterances.text: Yes, there were soldiers and these others who had come.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We've already explained how these came and how the soldiers left, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have -- we have dealt with this. We can return to it tomorrow morning. We're going to adjourn now because it's the time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. May, there's no need for this witness to come back tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We have to adjourn pretty promptly. Have you any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour, but if I could just point out two factual things: The statement that's been referred to, there's evidence that it was originated by a JNA or army soldier. In fact, the letterhead indicates it was a civilian commission set up by the Bosnian Presidency. And then the other thing I would just like to point out to the Chamber, in the other municipalities we've dealt with, the Drina has served as the border between Serbia and Bosnia. South of Srebrenica and in the Foca municipality, the Drina does not; it flows to the interior of Bosnia and it's Bosnia on both sides of the Drina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Taranin, that concludes your evidence. Thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You are now free to go. If you would wait until we've gone and then the blinds will be pulled down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 11th day of July, 2003, at 9.00 a.m.
